record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Determine the correct order of the best general lower bound for discrepancy that holds for all sequences in the d-dimensional unit cube [0,1)^d.

evidence.quote: determine the correct order of the best general lower bound for discrepancy, holding for all sequences in [0, 1)d

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an infinite sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge 1}$ in the $d$-dimensional unit cube $[0,1)^d$, define the star discrepancy of its first $N$ terms by
$$D_N^*(x_1,\dots,x_N) \;=\; \sup_{B}\left|\frac{\#\{1\le n\le N : x_n\in B\}}{N} - \mathrm{vol}(B)\right|,$$
where the supremum is taken over all axis-aligned boxes $B=\prod_{i=1}^d[0,a_i)\subseteq[0,1)^d$.

A classical theorem asserts that for every fixed $d\ge 1$ there exists a constant $c_d>0$ such that for every infinite sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge 1}$ in $[0,1)^d$,
$$N\,D_N^*(x_1,\dots,x_N) \;\ge\; c_d\,(\log N)^{\alpha(d)} \qquad \text{for infinitely many } N,$$
for some exponent $\alpha(d)$. The known constructions (e.g., Halton, digital $(t,d)$-sequences) show that there exist sequences with
$$N\,D_N^*(x_1,\dots,x_N) \;\le\; C_d\,(\log N)^{d} \qquad \text{for all } N\ge 2,$$
while the best general lower bound currently established is of order $(\log N)^{\beta(d)}$ with $\beta(d)<d$ for $d\ge 3$.

Problem. Determine the correct order of magnitude, as $N\to\infty$, of
$$\inf_{(x_n)_{n\ge 1}\subset[0,1)^d}\;\sup_{N\ge 2}\;\frac{N\,D_N^*(x_1,\dots,x_N)}{(\log N)^{s}},$$
i.e., find the precise exponent $s=s(d)$ such that the star discrepancy of every infinite sequence in $[0,1)^d$ satisfies $N\,D_N^*\gtrsim (\log N)^{s(d)}$ infinitely often, and such that this lower bound is sharp up to constants.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact order of the best general star-discrepancy lower bound for infinite sequences in $[0,1)^d$ remains open for $d\ge 3$. The conjectured order is $(\log N)^d$, matching known constructions, but the best known general lower bound (after work of Bilyk–Lacey–Vagharshakyan and others) is only of order $(\log N)^{(d-1)/2+\eta_d}$ for some small $\eta_d>0$. The analogous problem has been resolved for $L_p$-discrepancy ($1<p<\infty$), where the sharp order is $(\log N)^{d/2}$ (Proinov lower bound matched by Dick–Pillichshammer-type constructions), but the star (i.e., $L_\infty$) discrepancy case is still open.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems – Stefan Steinerberger
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectures on the optimal order of discrepancy of infinite sequences proved only for s ≤ 2 by W. M. Schmidt; in higher dimensions the corresponding problem is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The sharp lower bound on star discrepancy of infinite sequences in dimension d ≥ 3 is open.

status_evidence.title: Exact order of extreme L_p discrepancy of infinite sequences in arbitrary dimension
status_evidence.snippet: For any dimension d and any p>1, the extreme L_p discrepancy of every infinite sequence in [0,1)^d is at least of order (log N)^{d/2}, and this order is best possible.
status_evidence.claim: The L_p analogue (1<p<∞) is solved, but this does not settle the star (L_∞) discrepancy case.
